findings.evidence: "If the position counts as full-time, the stipend can apply... Only once every condition above is met does the home-office equipment stipend become available"
findings.fix: Rewrite as one conjunctive statement, e.g. "The stipend is available only if the position is full-time, the employee has completed 90 days of continuous service, and the request arrives before the benefit year ends."
findings.violation: Each of the three sentences states that satisfying a single condition alone makes the stipend "apply," but the closing sentence then requires all three together (AND), directly contradicting the independent "can apply" phrasing.

findings.evidence: "Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email."
findings.fix: Remove this anecdote or replace it with a general rule covering backup-reviewer notification when the primary manager is unavailable.
findings.location: How to Apply section, third paragraph
findings.violation: This is an anecdotal failure scenario, not a general policy rule, written as an unreadable run-on sentence, and it implicitly breaks the two-business-day SLA stated later without reconciling the two.

findings.evidence: "The request is reviewed within two business days."
findings.fix: Either remove the delay anecdote from "How to Apply" or add an explicit exception here for cases where the designated reviewer is unavailable.
findings.violation: This firm SLA directly conflicts with the preceding "How to Apply" section's scenario in which the backup reviewer is never notified and the review is delayed, with no exception noted.

findings.evidence: "The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: State the unit explicitly and align it, e.g. "an automatic reminder after three business days."
findings.violation: "Three days" is not tied to business or calendar days and is inconsistent with the "two business days" unit used one sentence earlier, leaving the timing ambiguous relative to the standard review period.

findings.evidence: "The manager approves items pursuant to internal discretion, notwithstanding the standard review checklist."
findings.fix: Decide whether approval is checklist-based, discretionary, or both, and state it consistently in both sections.
findings.violation: This states approval is discretionary regardless of the checklist, contradicting the Approval Timeline section's statement that "the manager confirms the equipment category matches the approved list," which is a checklist-based review.

findings.evidence: "Also, the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time."
findings.violation: This is circular filler - any reimbursement by definition offsets costs already paid - and "at this point in time" adds no information.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person, e.g. "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition; the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, first line
findings.violation: This switches to second-person ("You"/"we") voice, breaking from the third-person voice used elsewhere ("the employee," "the stipend"), and "we" is never identified.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with a neutral connector, or move this sentence into the Eligibility section.
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, second line
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies this rule is analogous to the prior sentence about photo checks, but a one-device-per-category limit is an unrelated eligibility rule, not a similar restriction.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: Convert to third person and reconcile the "each month" cadence with the earlier approval/deposit timelines.
findings.violation: This reintroduces the second-person "you" voice shift and adds a monthly reconciliation cadence for payroll release that conflicts with the two-business-day review and one-pay-cycle deposit timelines stated earlier.

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Remove this paragraph or merge it into "How to Apply."
findings.violation: This duplicates the portal-submission process already described in "How to Apply," adding no new information and scattering process documentation across sections.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Merge "Request Steps" into "How to Apply" as one consistent ordered list.
findings.violation: This contradicts "How to Apply," which describes the process as starting in the benefits portal with the portal walking through steps in order; the two sections give unreconciled accounts of what the process begins with and how many steps it has.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period."
findings.fix: Delete the duplicate "Overview" section and keep one consistent statement of who publishes the log and how often.
findings.location: second "## Overview" section (near end of document)
findings.violation: This duplicates the heading and topic of the earlier "Program Overview" section but contradicts it - there "the people operations office publishes the reimbursement log... each quarter," here it's the benefits team publishing it after open enrollment, a different owner and cadence for the same artifact.

findings.evidence: "Once approved, the team schedules the reimbursement for the next pay cycle."
findings.fix: Clarify which office is responsible for depositing/scheduling reimbursements and state it consistently in both sections.
findings.violation: This assigns scheduling of the reimbursement to "the benefits team," conflicting with "Reimbursement Amounts," which states "the finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle."

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: Integrate the $200 finance-review threshold into the Approval Timeline/Required Documentation sections so the full approval chain appears in one place.
findings.violation: This introduces a new $200 review threshold and an additional finance-office approval step never mentioned in "Approval Timeline" or "Required Documentation," leaving the overall approval chain incomplete and inconsistent.

findings.evidence: "The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Define "repeats" precisely, state what follows a flag, and reconcile this with the one-device-per-category rule.
findings.violation: "Repeats" is undefined, no resulting action is described, and this is in tension with the "one device per category per employee" restriction, which should already prevent most repeat requests.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team publishes the vendor list each quarter."
findings.fix: Rename the section to match its content (e.g., "Approved Vendor List") or replace the content with actual Q&A/update information.
findings.violation: The heading "Questions and Updates" promises FAQ or update content, but the body introduces an unrelated, previously undefined concept ("vendor list") with no connection to the rest of the policy.
